name: Strawberry and baking soda hack

lead: The strawberry and baking soda hack is a home remedy in which crushed strawberries are mixed with baking soda and applied to the teeth for a whiter look. It is promoted as a natural alternative to peroxide-based whitening.

Proponents say the fruit's malic acid lifts stains while the baking soda scrubs. No published studies on the mixture were found. Related literature covers baking soda as a mild abrasive and dietary acids as a cause of enamel erosion.

paras: People mash a strawberry, mix in baking soda and brush or rub it on the teeth for a short time before rinsing. It is used occasionally rather than daily and is usually shared as a quick, kitchen-ingredient trick. Users describe a fresher, cleaner look right after.

Dental erosion is described as irreversible loss of tooth structure from acids not of bacterial origin, with foods below roughly pH 5.0 to 5.7 able to trigger it. No safety data exist for the mixture itself.

angle.text: Users rub mashed strawberry and baking soda on teeth as a natural whitener, crediting the fruit's malic acid with loosening stain and the soda with scrubbing it off. It is a quick kitchen-ingredient routine. No studies on the mixture were found, and dental sources flag dietary acid as an erosion factor.

lead: The strawberry and baking soda hack is a do-it-yourself teeth-whitening remedy in which mashed strawberries are mixed with baking soda and applied to the teeth. It is promoted as a natural alternative to peroxide-based whitening.

No published studies of this mixture were found in the sources reviewed. Related background exists for its parts: baking soda has been described as a low-abrasive stain remover [1], and acidic foods and drinks are an established cause of dental erosion, defined as irreversible loss of tooth structure by non-bacterial acids [2].

Dental erosion sources describe foods and drinks below roughly pH 5.0 to 5.7 as capable of triggering erosion, and note that swishing acidic drinks or sucking citrus fruits is among behaviours to avoid [2].
infobox: Malic acid stain action; mild abrasion (as claimed by proponents)

paras: The remedy circulates on social media and wellness sites. Proponents say fruit acid and baking soda combine to whiten the teeth. No preparation instructions are given here.

Baking soda is described on Wikipedia, citing a 2017 review, as an effective low-abrasive stain remover [1]. Dietary acids, including fruit juices, are described as a cause of dental erosion, and frequency of exposure matters more than total volume [2].
No studies of strawberries, malic acid in strawberries, or this specific mixture for whitening were found.

lore.intro: The hack is discussed as a kitchen-ingredient whitening trick, popularised through short videos and wellness posts.

claims.claim: Strawberry malic acid plus baking soda whitens teeth
